children: South Korea's economy likely grew at a faster-than-expected pace in 3Q, Nomura's Jeong Woo Park says. The economist expects GDP to have expanded 1.6% from the previous quarter and 4.0% from a year earlier for the July-September period, sharply above his earlier forecasts of 0.1% on quarter growth and 2.4% on year growth. Park raises his full-year 2026 growth forecast to 3.6% from 3.2%. Strong exports of artificial intelligence-related products, including chips and computers, likely contributed substantially to 3Q growth, while the global AI investment cycle supported domestic facilities investment, particularly in semiconductors, he says. "These gains continue to offset weakness in household consumption," he adds. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
